reason: Attacked and it held, with two things for the editor. I downloaded Project Gutenberg 3600, Cotton as revised by W. Carew Hazlitt, and read the sentence in place at lines 44448 to 44453, inside CHAPTER IX, OF VANITY at line 43176, which falls after BOOK THE THIRD at line 36159, so Book III chapter 9 is correct, and the volume title page carries 1877. The edition reads: Besides these reasons, travel is in my opinion a very profitable exercise; the soul is there continually employed in observing new and unknown things, and I do not know, as I have often said a better school wherein to model life than by incessantly exposing to it the diversity of so many other lives, fancies, and usances, and by making it relish a perpetual variety of forms of human nature. The two readings I most suspected are the edition's own and not drift: there is no comma after said, and it is a perpetual variety, not the so perpetual variety of some other renderings. The card drops the four opening words and raises travel to a capital, which is quotation practice and mints nothing.
